channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques conhece iniciativas do TRE-PR voltadas à inclusão indígena e à modernização da Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques visited the TRE-PR for the first time since assuming office and praised its Indigenous Peoples Ombudsman, established by Resolution No. 978/2026, as a vanguard initiative to ensure full participation of approximately 5,5 thousand indigenous people in elections. He emphasized that the ombudsman is essential to overcome information access and linguistic barriers, guaranteeing transparent and effective service for indigenous communities. The initiative was praised by indigenous leaders and Funai experts as a key step toward increasing indigenous representation as voters, polling officials, and candidates.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia R$ 225 mi para equipamentos do SUS
item.description: President Lula announced a R$225 million investment to purchase 150 surgical equipment kits for the SUS, benefiting 138 municipalities nationwide. The initiative, under the Agora Tem Especialistas program, aims to modernize public health procedures, reduce hospitalization time and post-operative complications, while stimulating the domestic health industry. Additional deliveries included 406 patient transport vehicles, 87 mobile dental units, 10 Samu 192 ambulances, a tomograph for Aracaju’s Cancer Hospital, and R$30 million for a polyclinic in Lagarto to serve 260,000 people.

item.title: Fux rejeita pedido da Alerj e mantém Ricardo Couto no comando do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux rejected the request from the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly (Alerj) to replace interim Governor Ricardo Couto with Assembly President Douglas Ruas, upholding the injunction that keeps Couto in office. The decision rests on the STF collegiate’s express determination and the pending joint judgment of ADI 7942 and Rcl 92644, which was stalled by a view request from Minister Flávio Dino. Ruas, a 2026 gubernatorial pre-candidate backed by Flávio Bolsonaro, saw his indirect succession bid denied due to the Liberal Party’s lack of standing as amicus curiae in the case.

item.title: Com Lula fora de Brasília, ministros fazem balanço de decisão dos EUA sobre CV e PCC
item.description: Lula's ministers convened to assess the impact of the U.S. decision to designate PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, discussing effects on financial markets, public security, and tourism. Lula directed his team to evaluate financial and international cooperation impacts, requested support from the IMF and World Bank, and reaffirmed national sovereignty, rejecting foreign intervention. He also criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for urging the U.S. to label the groups as terrorists, accusing him of betraying the nation.

item.title: Ataque eleitoral vai prejudicar economia brasileira, diz Durigan após classificação de PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan labeled the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations as an 'electoral attack' that could harm Brazil's economy, particularly the financial system and Pix. He argued the move is driven by foreign interests and the Bolsonaro family, but affirmed the government will defend Brazil's instant payment system, ensuring no harm to Pix usage by Brazilians.

item.title: Rede pede que STF suspenda mudanças na Lei da Ficha Limpa até conclusão de julgamento
item.description: The Sustainability Network (Rede Sustentabilidade) has asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to immediately suspend the congressional amendments to the Clean Record Law (Ficha Limpa) that changed the calculation of ineligibility periods from post-sentence to conviction date, pending the Court’s final ruling on their constitutionality. The party argues that legal uncertainty undermines electoral integrity by creating confusion over candidate eligibility during conventions, registration, and voting in the 2026 general elections. Prior to Justice Gilmar Mendes’ request for vista, Justices Cármen Lúcia and Luiz Fux had already voted to declare the amendments unconstitutional, stating they undermine administrative probity and risk enabling impunity.

item.title: Baleia Rossi confirma apoio do MDB no Senado ao fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Baleia Rossi, president of the MDB, confirmed the party's support in the Senate for a constitutional amendment reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, to be implemented in phases: 42 hours after 60 days and 40 hours after 14 months from promulgation. The proposal passed the Chamber of Deputees with strong majorities (472 in favor in the first round, 461 in the second). The announcement was made at a LIDE business lunch in São Paulo, attended by former president Michel Temer, São Paulo mayor Ricardo Nunes, and vice-governor Felicio Ramuth.

item.title: Lula visita primeiro hospital oncológico interestadual do país
item.description: President Lula visited the Interstate Cancer Hospital of Lagarto, Brazil's first interstate oncology facility, while undergoing radiotherapy for a scalp lesion. He emphasized equal access to advanced medical technology through the SUS, defended national sovereignty, and rejected U.S. labeling of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorists. The hospital serves 2.9 million people across four Northeastern states with R$137.5 million in federal funding.

item.title: Lula conversa com senadores para tentar pavimentar o caminho de Messias ao STF
item.description: President Lula has been personally involved in efforts to renominate Attorney General Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court following his previous defeat in the Senate vote. He has been speaking with various senators to smooth the path for the nomination and avoid surprises, publicly stating he will resend the nomination. Messias has remained silent on the matter but reportedly spoke with 79 of 81 senators prior to the earlier vote.

item.title: O salário que o PL vai pagar a Cláudio Castro
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro agreed to a BRL 38,000 salary with the PL party, funded by electoral and party funds, before being targeted by Federal Police operations. He announced he will no longer run for the Senate, stating he must focus on his legal defense and law practice, after reinstating his OAB license. Castro is ineligible due to a TSE ruling for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections and now faces two simultaneous PF investigations.

item.title: Nunes diz que EUA podem interferir se for para prender membros do PCC
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) supported potential U.S. intervention to arrest members of the PCC and Comando Vermelho after the U.S. designated the groups as terrorist organizations. He criticized President Lula’s claim that the move undermines Brazilian sovereignty, stating that true sovereignty lies in the people’s freedom to live without criminal violence. The remarks were made at the Lide Business Lunch, which discussed political scenarios ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula exibe cicatriz de tratamento contra câncer durante visita em Sergipe
item.description: President Lula displayed the scar from skin cancer removal on his scalp during a visit to the Hospital of Amor in Lagarto, Sergipe. He spoke with patients, removed his hat to show the mark, and stated he is also undergoing treatment, emphasizing prevention and healthcare access.

item.title: Bolsonaros querem fragilizar soberania nacional, diz Boulos
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol) accused Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and his family of attempting to weaken national sovereignty by urging the U.S. to label Brazil’s PCC and CV criminal groups as narcoterrorists, arguing this serves U.S. interests, not Brazil’s fight against crime. He noted that President Lula had already requested the extradition of fugitive criminals from the U.S. and criticized Bolsonarism for acting in favor of the United States, citing events such as the large U.S. flag on Paulista Avenue and tariff proposals that would harm Brazilian jobs.

item.title: Fux nega pedido do presidente da Alerj para assumir o governo do Rio
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux rejected a petition by state deputy Douglas Ruas (PL), president of the Alerj, to assume the governorship of Rio de Janeiro, upholding interim Governor Ricardo Couto’s role until the court decides on the format of a supplementary election. Fux stated that the Court’s plenary had already ruled to block consideration of the Alerj’s request, and that any new developments would be reviewed by the full bench. This marks Ruas’s second failed attempt to take over the Guanabara Palace, following an earlier denial by Justice Cristiano Zanin.

item.title: Trump dá sua contribuição à agenda de Flávio Bolsonaro, à qual Lula terá dificuldade de contrapor
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro sought support in the United States, particularly from Marco Rubio and JD Vance, to pressure the Trump administration to designate PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, aiming to use this alliance with Trump as an electoral asset. This move puts Lula in a difficult position, as he has historically opposed such foreign interference and now faces pressure to take a stance on reclassifying these criminal factions, risking accusations of 'protecting criminals' in an election year where security is a decisive issue.

item.title: Fux nega pedido de Douglas Ruas para assumir governo do Rio interinamente
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Luiz Fux denied a request by state deputy Douglas Ruas (PL), president of the Alerj, to assume the interim governorship of Rio de Janeiro. The decision upholds Judge Ricardo Couto as interim governor, as previously determined by the STF, pending judgment on challenges to the state’s indirect election model. The governorship has been vacant since Claudio Castro’s resignation in March 2026 following his ineligibility ruling by the TSE, and after the prior resignation of Vice Governor Thiago Pampolha in 2025.

item.title: Messias representará Lula na Marcha para Jesus pelo quarto ano seguido
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias confirmed his participation in the March for Jesus in São Paulo, scheduled for Thursday (4). This will be his fourth consecutive appearance at the event since 2023, the start of Lula's government. The confirmation reinforces the federal government's outreach to evangelical movements.

item.title: Ibovespa recua e acumula queda de quase 7% em maio
item.description: The Ibovespa closed May down 0.73% on Friday, accumulating a 6.81% decline for the month, driven by foreign capital outflows, weaker Brazilian GDP data, and fiscal uncertainty in an election year. Banking stocks led losses, with Banco do Brasil (BBAS3) falling 1.50% and Bradesco (BBDC4) dropping 1.12%, while Itaú (ITUB4) edged up 0.10%. The dollar closed slightly lower at BRL 5.00, reflecting a sideways FX market due to high interest rates, limited foreign inflows, and lack of new catalysts.

item.title: Nunes nomeia Renata Gil para diretoria internacional do TSE
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques appointed Judge Renata Gil Alcântara to lead the International Affairs Directorate of the court, per Portaria 256 of 2026. Gil, a magistrate from TJ-RJ since 1998 and former president of the AMB, leaves her role as advisor to Judge Ricardo Couto to assume the position in Brasília, focusing on international articulation, external agenda management, and monitoring international observer missions for the October municipal elections. She emphasized the importance of female representation in decision-making spaces and described the Electoral Justice as a soft power instrument for Brazil.

item.title: Fachin não reage a ação de Dino que deixou só 1 candidato em Roraima
item.description: STF President Edson Fachin did not comment on Minister Flávio Dino’s decision to override the TRE-RR’s rules for Roraima’s supplementary election, imposing a six-month disaffiliation period. This left acting Governor Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos) as the sole viable candidate, as no other contender could meet the new requirement given the election’s emergency scheduling for June 21, 2026. Dino’s ruling ignored established jurisprudence and the 58 prior supplementary elections that relaxed the deadline, benefiting only Sampaio, an ally of the MDB and former Senator Romero Jucá.

item.title: Fux nega pedido de Douglas Ruas para assumir governo do Rio no lugar de Ricardo Couto
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Luiz Fux denied a request by Douglas Ruas, president of the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly, to assume the state government on an interim basis. Fux stated that the STF plenary has expressly determined that Ricardo Couto, president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice, must continue as acting governor until a new decision by the full court. He added that any new facts, such as Ruas’s election as Alerj president, will be submitted to the plenary’s consideration in due course.

item.title: ‘Bondades’ de Lula não evitam desaceleração da economia
item.description: Brazil's economy is expected to slow down in 2026 after a better-than-expected first-quarter performance, according to economists consulted by Folha. The slowdown is attributed to the continued high benchmark interest rate, which is pressuring growth despite government stimulus measures dubbed Lula's 'bondades'.

item.title: TSE marca para 2 de junho o julgamento do recurso de Castro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) scheduled June 2, 2026, to rule on the appeal of Cláudio Castro (PL), former governor of Rio de Janeiro, who was declared ineligible until 2030 for abuse of power in the 2022 elections. Castro resigned on May 28 to meet incompatibilization requirements and withdrew his Senate pre-candidacy, creating a succession vacuum that prompted the TSE to mandate indirect elections by the state legislature. The PSD challenged the decision at the STF, advocating for direct elections, while the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice appointed Ricardo Couto de Castro as interim governor pending the electoral format determination.

item.title: Adoecer na cidade e a exaustão da vida urbana
item.description: Illness in Brazilian peripheries, such as Salvador’s Subúrbio Ferroviário, stems not only from lack of healthcare access but from unequal urban distribution of infrastructure, housing, mobility, sanitation, and protection — producing physical and emotional exhaustion. The testimony of Rosângela, a nursing technician and periphery resident, reveals how urban life — marked by crowded transport, fear, and long commutes — undermines health before hospital arrival. The text argues that democratic reconstruction requires socially just and environmentally viable cities, where territorialized care is a priority.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: pré-candidatos podem realizar propaganda intrapartidária a partir de 5 de julho
item.description: Starting July 5, pre-candidates may conduct intraparty propaganda for the 2026 elections, per TSE Resolution No. 23.610/2019. Electoral advertising on radio, TV, and internet begins only on August 16. Party conventions, which set candidates and coalitions, run from July 20 to August 5.

item.title: Clica e Confirma destaca criação de comissão permanente para tratar de IA na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: The TSE announced the creation of a permanent commission to address the use of artificial intelligence within the Electoral Justice system, planning to establish units in the Regional Electoral Courts (TREs) to monitor and discuss AI use in the 2026 elections. Additionally, the TSE made the source code of electronic voting machines and electoral systems available for inspection by oversight entities, with the União Brasil party being the first to conduct such an audit. The program also highlighted the electoral calendar, noting June 1st as a key deadline for political parties, and reported over one million Brazilian voters abroad registered with the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Porta-voz dos EUA nega influência de Flávio e diz que é improvável reverter decisão sobre PCC e CV
item.description: U.S. State Department spokesperson Amanda Roberson stated that the designation of PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations is unlikely to be reversed and was not influenced by Brazilian politicians, including Flávio Bolsonaro. She emphasized the decision was made independently by the Trump administration after months of review and will not lead to military action or sanctions against companies without ties to the groups.

item.title: O aceno de Ciro Gomes às pretensões de Aécio concorrer à presidência
item.description: The PSDB's pre-candidate for governor of Ceará, Ciro Gomes, expressed support for Aécio Neves, national president of the PSDB, to run for president in 2026. Although he was probed to be a presidential candidate and felt tempted, Ciro chose to remain in the race for the Palácio da Abolição. In a statement, he emphasized the importance of Aécio's candidacy in the current context of ideological polarization, advocating for moderation, balance, and conciliation to address Brazil's social, economic, and international challenges.

item.title: Governo brasileiro tem dia de reuniões para avaliar possíveis implicações da decisão dos EUA sobre facções
item.description: The Brazilian government convened to assess the implications of the U.S. decision to designate PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations. Lula defended national sovereignty, rejecting any pretext for external intervention, and requested analyses on impacts to international cooperation and finances. The meeting included ministers from the Civil Cabinet, Foreign Relations, Finance, Justice, and the Presidential Advisory Office.

item.title: ‘É um erro atribuir isso ao Flávio’, diz ex-embaixador sobre decisão de Trump
item.description: Former ambassador Rubens Barbosa stated that the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations was already part of America's national security strategy, and that Flávio Bolsonaro's meeting with Trump was merely a final push, not the main cause. He warned the PT against giving Flávio sole credit, as it could boost his electoral standing. The move raised Brazilian concerns about potential U.S. sanctions on companies and the payment system, with economic, diplomatic, and electoral implications.

item.title: Nem Lula nem Flávio, quem vai ganhar o debate sobre facções terroristas são os marqueteiros
item.description: The 2026 election will not be won by Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro, but by marketers who can turn the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorists into emotionally resonant narratives that reflect the Brazilian voter’s contradiction: demanding security without sacrificing dignity. The winner will be the one who crafts a 30-second video balancing state force with social justice — like a well-lit bus stop and respectful policing — capturing the Reels of Dona Edcléia and, with it, the election.

item.title: Por que o governo vê risco ao Pix após EUA classificarem PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: The Brazilian government is concerned about potential U.S. sanctions on Pix following the designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, fearing that allegations of money laundering facilitation could be used to target the payment system. Two ministers expressed alarm, describing the risk as 'tremendous gravity' and 'imminent', with the issue treated as sensitive and highly visible. The government's official statement warns that unilateral U.S. actions could weaken crime-fighting efforts, reduce police cooperation, and threaten national innovations like Pix.

item.title: ‘Traidores e falsos patriotas’: a dura nota do governo Lula após decisão dos EUA sobre CV e PCC
item.description: The Lula government condemned the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations as a violation of Brazilian sovereignty, accusing 'traitors' and 'false patriots' of colluding with organized crime to seek foreign interference. The statement implicitly targets the Bolsonaro family, citing Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro’s meeting with Trump prior to the announcement, and warns of potential sanctions on Brazil’s financial system and Pix payment mechanism.

item.title: ‘Há espaço para uma alternativa’, afirma Eduardo Leite após crise envolvendo Flávio com Vorcaro
item.description: Rio Grande do Sul Governor Eduardo Leite stated that the controversy involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former banker Daniel Vorcaro creates ongoing wear and opens space for an alternative in the 2026 presidential race, breaking the polarization between lulism and bolsonarism. He emphasized the need for a debate focused on concrete national proposals rather than mere opposition to adversaries, and expressed support for pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado of the PSD, citing his honored public service record.

item.title: Decisão de Trump sobre facções não ajuda no combate ao crime, diz Alessandro Vieira
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) stated that the Trump administration's designation of the PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations is a political move with no practical impact on fighting organized crime, as current Brazilian legislation and cooperation with U.S. authorities are sufficient. He criticized the measure as a way to justify military intervention in sovereign nations. Lula called Flávio Bolsonaro a 'traitor' for his alignment with the U.S. government.

item.title: Pacheco desiste de disputar governo de Minas e diz que vai sair da política
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) announced he will not run for governor of Minas Gerais in 2026 and intends to leave politics at the end of his term, removing the name Lula considered key to lead a progressive ticket in the state’s pivotal election. His withdrawal follows political tensions tied to the succession at the Supreme Court and divisions between government allies and Senate leaders, deepening uncertainty over Lula’s coalition in Minas Gerais, a strategic state for the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Alcolumbre acena para a oposição com PDLs de redes sociais e aborto, além de reação à 6×1
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre advanced the processing of bills challenging the Lula government, including a PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule and four PDLs seeking to overturn the digital platforms responsibility decree, plus a PDL aiming to block abortion guidelines for minor victims of sexual violence. Despite lacking prior agreement with the opposition, Alcolumbre expedited proposals by Rogério Marinho, exposing the Planalto to potential sensitive legislative defeats.

item.title: Cotada para ser ministra de Flávio diz que eleição será decidida pelas mulheres
item.description: Daniella Marques, former president of Caixa Econômica Federal and a potential candidate for Minister of Economy in a possible Flávio Bolsonaro government, said the 2026 elections will be decided by women. She made the remark during a meeting with business leaders, emphasizing the decisive role of female voters in the electoral outcome.

item.title: Edinho diz que recusa de Pacheco criou 'problema' para o PT e que vai a MG conversar com Kalil
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva announced he will travel to Minas Gerais to meet with allies and pre-candidate for governor Alexandre Kalil (PDT) to discuss renewing the alliance with Lula in 2026, following Senator Rodrigo Pacheco's refusal to support the PT ticket in the state, which Silva said created a 'problem' for the party.

item.title: Lula compreenderá a minha saída da política, afirma Rodrigo Pacheco
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) says President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will understand his decision to leave politics, emphasizing that there is nothing new about his choice and that Lula, due to his experience, will be able to comprehend it.

item.title: 'Presidente do Brasil é escolha dos brasileiros', diz porta-voz do Departamento de Estado dos EUA
item.description: Amanda Roberson, spokesperson for the U.S. Department of State in Brazil, stated that the choice of Brazil's president is solely up to Brazilians, rejecting any possibility of U.S. intervention in the elections. She emphasized that U.S. priorities are strengthening its own economy and security, and that the U.S. will not seek to influence Brazil's electoral process, even after designating the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Presidente do TSE diz que tecnologia não ameaça democracia, mas defende regras contra fraudes
item.description: The president of the TSE, Minister Kássio Nunes Marques, stated that technology itself does not threaten democracy, but advocated for objective rules to combat fraud using artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections. He emphasized the need to balance freedom of expression with electoral integrity, acknowledging that the speed of disinformation often outpaces institutional response capacity.

item.title: Boulos questiona se EUA classificarão milícias do RJ como terroristas
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos questioned whether the United States will also designate Rio de Janeiro’s militias linked to the Bolsonaros as terrorist organizations, following the State Department’s announcement that the PCC and CV will be classified as foreign terrorist organizations effective June 5. He noted the timing of the announcement shortly after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, implying potential political influence on the U.S. decision.

item.title: Bolsonaro orienta Flávio a explorar tema das facções após decisão dos EUA sobre PCC e CV, dizem aliados
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro advised Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to leverage the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations to bolster the public security agenda in his pre-campaign and criticize the Lula government. The advice was given during a meeting at the Solar de Brasília condominium after Flávio returned from Washington, where he met with Donald Trump. The strategy aims to reposition the Bolsonarist campaign after internal setbacks and define the party's candidate for the Rio de Janeiro Senate race.

item.title: Caiado diz que decisão sobre facções deveria ter sido tomada mais cedo pelo próprio governo brasileiro
item.description: PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized the federal government for not acting sooner against organized crime, stating that the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as global terrorist organizations should have been made by Brazil earlier. He warned of lost sovereignty due to criminal factions controlling territory, citing 50 million Brazilians living under a 'crime state' and foreign drug cartels infiltrating the Amazon. Caiado advocated for harsher penalties and warned about money laundering in the formal economy and criminals infiltrating public institutions.

item.title: Lula diz que assinou mais 2 decretos para conter alta dos combustíveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced he signed two additional decrees to curb fuel price increases amid rising oil prices due to the Middle East war. He stated the measures, including subsidies and federal tax exemptions, aim to prevent losses at Petrobras and keep fuel prices low in Brazil. Lula also criticized the 2021 privatization of BR Distribuidora, arguing that state absence in fuel distribution harms the country during international instability.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro ganha fôlego com medida de Trump sobre PCC e CV, mas não reverte desgaste do Master
item.description: The Trump administration's designation of PCC and CV as international terrorist organizations had a positive impact on Flávio Bolsonaro's image on social media, increasing positive mentions by 2.9 percentage points and reducing negative mentions from 70.2% to 62.5%. However, the reputational damage from revelations about his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro was not fully reversed, as negative mentions remain above the 57.5% level before the Master case. Confidence in the senator remains low, rising from 10.33% to 12.2% after the announcement but declining again this morning.

item.title: A reação de Lula à decisão dos EUA de declarar CV e PCC como 'terroristas': 'Não aceitamos ser tratados como moleques'
item.description: President Lula rejected the U.S. designation of CV and PCC as terrorist organizations, stating Brazil will not be treated like a 'banana republic' or 'kid'. He defended national sovereignty in defining crime and noted he had previously given Trump a document on organized crime combat during his White House visit.

item.title: Família Bolsonaro prejudica investidores e empresas, diz Edinho Silva
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva claimed the Bolsonaro family harms Brazilian investors and companies by seeking international support for crime-fighting agendas, which he says undermines national sovereignty. He specifically criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for urging the U.S. to label PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, calling it foreign interference. He defended Lula’s government for combating crime through intelligence and institutional cooperation without sacrificing Brazil’s autonomy.

item.title: Crusoé: O populismo da PEC 6×1
item.description: The vote on PEC 6×1 in the Chamber of Deputies revealed that the proposal has moved beyond a labor debate to become an early political platform for the government’s base ahead of the 2026 elections. Lula-aligned deputies used the issue to mobilize popular support and consolidate narratives defending workers, turning the reform into an electoral capital instrument.
